text:
fran: hey all, first-day problem: I can `ssh jump@bastion` from Terminal and then `ssh internal-host` fine, but VS Code Remote-SSH keeps failing with 'Permission denied (publickey)' when trying to connect to internal-host via the bastion. I configured ProxyJump in my ~/.ssh/config:```Host bastion
  HostName bastion.internal.redwood.internal
  User jump
Host internal-host
  HostName internal-host.internal.redwood.internal
  User fran
  ProxyJump bastion
  ForwardAgent yes```
Any ideas? :confused:

it-ops: welcome! first guess: VS Code ships its own ssh binary inside the app bundle which doesn't see your ssh-agent socket or macOS Keychain-managed keys. A couple quick checks: 1) can you `ssh -A internal-host` from Terminal without password prompts? 2) in VS Code Remote-SSH output, is it trying "/usr/bin/ssh" or the bundled one?

fran: yes `ssh -A internal-host` from Terminal works, agent forwarding is fine. In the VS Code logs I see it's invoking `"/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/remote-ssh/dist/bin/remote-ssh"` then later a path to a vendor ssh. Not super clear.

devex: common issue — VS Code's remote extension can use its own SSH or the system SSH depending on settings. Try setting `remote.SSH.path` to the system ssh and enable local server. Steps: 1) open Command Palette -> Preferences: Open Settings (JSON) and add:```"remote.SSH.path": "/usr/bin/ssh",
"remote.SSH.useLocalServer": true
```2) reload VS Code. That makes VS Code call the system ssh which sees your agent and ProxyJump config.

maya: also confirm VS Code can access the SSH_AUTH_SOCK. If you're using a GUI launch (dock click) on macOS, the environment may not include your agent socket. Launching VS Code from terminal (`code .`) usually inherits the env. Alternatively, add the agent socket to launchd env via a small plist or use the macOS Keychain helper (`ssh-add -K`) on older macOS. On Sonoma/Apple Silicon we recommend `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain` where supported.

it-ops: one more quirk: some GUI git clients (e.g., GitHub Desktop, Tower) or VS Code built-in Git may ignore ProxyJump and use libssh/libgit2 which doesn't read your ~/.ssh/config. If you rely on VS Code's Git features against internal repos, either configure an HTTPS remote for initial clone or add a local `~/.ssh/config` entry that sets `IdentityFile` and `ProxyCommand` explicitly, e.g.:```Host internal-host
  HostName internal-host.internal.redwood.internal
  User fran
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_rsa_redwood
  ProxyCommand ssh -W %h:%p bastion
```
This makes non-OpenSSH libs that do read config more likely to connect.

fran: updated settings to use /usr/bin/ssh and launched VS Code from terminal — Remote-SSH started the host install and connected! :tada: I did have to `ssh-add -K ~/.ssh/id_rsa_redwood` to ensure the key was available to GUI apps.

devex: great. we'll add a short onboarding note: "If using VS Code Remote-SSH, set remote.SSH.path to /usr/bin/ssh and prefer launching VS Code from terminal so SSH_AUTH_SOCK is inherited; for GUI-only workflows add keys to macOS keychain or set IdentityFile in ~/.ssh/config."

devex-bot: created ticket #INFR-4010 to add VS Code Remote-SSH troubleshooting (ProxyJump, system ssh path, agent visibility) to the new-hire docs and checklist.

maya: also ping us if you need a copy of the `id_rsa_redwood` upload instructions for GitLab/Bitbucket internal; we can pre-provision keys for managed devices. :+1:
